questions.q: Why can't a plain SELECT * against raw_customers answer "what was this customer's status last quarter"?
options: SELECT * is not valid syntax in Snowflake
raw_customers only ever holds the current value — history is lost the moment a row is overwritten, with nothing recording what it used to be
raw_customers does not contain a status column at all
Snowflake automatically deletes old rows after 90 days
questions.explain: Without a snapshot, only the current status is ever visible — there's no mechanism recording what changed or when.

questions.q: What does strategy='timestamp' tell dbt to do in a snapshot config?
options: Delete rows older than the configured timestamp
Compare each row's updated_at column against what's already recorded, inserting a new snapshot row whenever that timestamp has moved forward
Run the snapshot only once, at the timestamp specified in config
Automatically convert all timestamps to UTC
questions.explain: The timestamp strategy detects changes by comparing the named updated_at column, not by hashing or comparing every column.

questions.q: What is unique_key='customer_id' for in the snapshot config?
options: It sets the warehouse used to run the snapshot
It's how dbt knows which snapshot rows across multiple runs belong to the same real-world customer
It enforces a NOT NULL constraint on customer_id
It determines the snapshot's target schema name
questions.explain: unique_key identifies the real-world entity each snapshot row represents, letting dbt track that entity's history across runs.

questions.q: What do dbt_valid_from and dbt_valid_to let you do with a snapshotted table?
options: Nothing useful — they're internal bookkeeping columns with no analytical value
Reconstruct exactly which version of a row was current during any past time window, answering real historical questions
Automatically delete expired snapshot rows
Force a snapshot to re-run from scratch
questions.explain: A row with a real dbt_valid_to and one with dbt_valid_to IS NULL together reconstruct a queryable history of exactly when each version was current.

questions.q: Why is a snapshot described in this lesson as a governance artifact, not just a technical feature?
options: Because it's the platform's version-controlled answer to "can we reconstruct history," instead of relying on someone having exported a manual backup
Because snapshots require ACCOUNTADMIN privileges to create
Because snapshots automatically enforce RBAC on every table
Snapshots have no connection to governance in this lesson
questions.explain: The snapshot answers a real governance question — can history be reconstructed — in version-controlled SQL rather than ad hoc backups.
